LESSON: GROUPING OF FOOD

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES
Strand: Foods
Topic 3.4: Grouping of food

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grouping of food. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What foods do we get (4 lessons) learner should be able to: identify foods they get from from plants?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples
2. describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment
3. practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food
4. tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GROUPING OF FOOD
Subject: HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grouping of food helps you succeed in HYGIENE AND NUTRITION ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: GROUPING OF FOOD
Grouping of food is part of Science learning. Connect every idea to something you can observe.
Use safe examples only. Do not try dangerous experiments without a teacher.
Write definitions in your own words, then add one drawing or real-life example.

PART 1: Explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Grouping of food” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment

What this means
In this part you learn to describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Grouping of food matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food

What this means
In this part you learn to practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Grouping of food this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Grouping of food” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grouping of food is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Grouping of food” around your school. (skill: explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples)

Example 2: Say why Grouping of food matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Grouping of food this week. (skill: practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food)

Example 4: Name what you can see/touch about “Grouping of food” around your school. (skill: tell why Grouping of food matters for life in Kenya)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grouping of food to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples.
3. Practise this skill: describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment.
4. Practise this skill: practise one safe skill connected to Grouping of food.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grouping of food from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grouping of food: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Grouping of food?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What foods do we get (4 lessons) learner should be able to: identify foods they get from from plants?
2. What foods do we get they come from, plant they come from (leaves, from animals?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grouping of food means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Grouping of food means using everyday Kenyan examples.
5. Be able to: describe how Grouping of food appears at home, school, or in the environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
